name: Ben Tre
provinceNote: Nghị quyết 202/2025/QH15, clause 20: Bến Tre, Trà Vinh, and Vĩnh Long become the new Vĩnh Long province, 6,296.20 km² and 4,257,581 people, beside Đồng Tháp, Cần Thơ, and the sea.
dotReason: Worth a night when the coconut bank of the Tiền is the trip
summary: A Mekong town of coconut canals and river islets. Take a boat through the palm creeks to Con Phung and Con Quy, and eat coconut candy at the kiln. A day and a night on the south bank of the Tien is the stay.
getThere: 86 km and 1.5 hours, about two hours, about 85 km and about 2 hours, or 85–90 km and 1.5–2 hours from Ho Chi Minh City. No passenger train.
seoTitle: Ben Tre travel guide — coconut canals and the islets
seoDescription: Stay for the coconut palms, Cồn Phụng, and Hồ Trúc Giang. The road from Ho Chi Minh City is 86 km and 1.5 hours, about two hours, or 85–90 km and 1.5–2 hours.
intro: You come for the coconut canals and the islets. You are on the south bank of the Tiền, on cù lao Bảo, with coconut palms in front of the town and boats leaving the pier into nipa creeks. Bảo is one of three strips the national rural page names, with Minh and An Hóa, cut by the Tiền, Hàm Luông, Ba Lai, and Cổ Chiên. Stay the night if that coconut bank is the trip. Sleep in My Tho if you wanted the north-bank embankment. The boat has to be the morning on a same-day return. The investment sheet says 86 km and 1.5 hours by car on the Ho Chi Minh City–Trung Lương expressway. Vietnam Tourism says about two hours. A travel page says about 85 km and about 2 hours. A car-hire page says 85–90 km and 1.5–2 hours.

Cồn Phụng is the orchard gate on this bank, not cù lao Thới Sơn. The national rural page places it in xã Tân Thạch, huyện Châu Thành, 12 km by road and 25 km by river from the city center. The operator page says about 10 km, and the address ấp 10 (Ấp Tân Vinh), xã Phú Túc, tỉnh Vĩnh Long. Clause 59 of Nghị quyết 1687/NQ-UBTVQH15 merges thị trấn Châu Thành and the communes Tân Thạch, Tường Đa, and Phú Túc into xã Phú Túc. Ask for either name. The clause does not say the islet moved. The four nicknames are Long, Lân, Quy, and Phụng. Vietnam Tourism places Cù lao Long on this side, by a short ferry past the Ben Tre Market and the Ben Tre River. Lân is not assigned a bank. Quy is a longan orchard. The Friday town cart is not the way onto the islet.

The morning the provincial tourism site describes starts on đường 30 Tháng 4, then walks to Bảo tàng Bến Tre at 146 Hùng Vương. The site says phường An Hội. A travel page says Phường 3 for the same number. Phường 4 and Phường 5 merged into An Hội from 1 December 2024, and clause 116 of Nghị quyết 1687 forms a new phường An Hội without naming Hùng Vương, so the number stays 146 Hùng Vương. One travel page says 07:00–17:00 every day. Another says 07:30–11:00 and 13:30–17:00. After dinner the site walks Hồ Trúc Giang, công viên Bến Tre, công viên Trần Văn Ơn, and công viên Đồng Khởi, then chợ đêm Bến Tre and khu phố chợ Phú Khương. Công viên Đồng Khởi in town is not the Đồng Khởi relic at Định Thủy.

The palms are the crop, and the area figures do not match. The national tourism extract says 53,000 ha, about a quarter of the country’s coconut land, and about 500 million nuts a year. The rural page says more than 60,000 ha and about 500 million nuts. Báo Đồng Khởi, writing in 2019 about the 2015 festival, says the area was above 62,000 ha. All three areas stand. An English article from the national rural tourism center, with no date on the article, says over 200,000 ha, nearly half of the country’s coconut land. That fourth area stands with them. Candy, milk, oil, and shell craft are the products. The rural page says more than 500 coconut-shell objects. Vietnam Tourism says more than 300 coconut-candy factories. The provincial tourism site, 25 November 2024, says more than 180 workshops. Both counts stand.
gettingAround: The road from Ho Chi Minh City is the approach, and Tân Sơn Nhất is the airport at that end. Do not plan a train. Tourist boats start once you are already on the river.

Vietnam Tourism says local buses connect the delta provinces with Bến xe Miền Tây and names Thảo Châu as one company to Ben Tre. The investment sheet names Quốc lộ 60 and Quốc lộ 57 as the roads that continue toward the old Vĩnh Long and Trà Vinh.

From My Tho, Quốc lộ 60 crosses the Tiền on Cầu Rạch Miễu and on Cầu Rạch Miễu 2. The state inspection page says Cầu Rạch Miễu 2 was ready to open from 19 August 2025, after a check on 12 August: more than 17.6 km in all, main bridge more than 1,971 m, investment more than 6,810 billion VND, from ngã tư Đồng Tâm in Đồng Tháp to Quốc lộ 60 in Vĩnh Long. VOV gives the length as about 17.6 km, the end near Km16+660, about 0.71 km from the north abutment of Cầu Hàm Luông, old TP. Bến Tre, now phường Bến Tre, and the start now xã Hưng Long, Đồng Tháp. Tuổi Trẻ gives the opening at about 11:30 on 19 August 2025, and the older bridge about 4 km downstream, still open that day. The temporary ferry stopped on 20 August 2025. The two “about 10 km” lines describe that ferry, not the drive from My Tho.

In town the walk is Hồ Trúc Giang and the three parks, then the night market and khu phố chợ Phú Khương. The near-city orchard boats leave bến tàu du lịch thành phố Bến Tre. Cồn Phụng is a different landing: 12 km by road and 25 km by river, or about 10 km. On Fridays and Saturdays the tourism site gives a free seven-seat cart, pickup at Sense City at 17:30 and 19:30 and at 708 Nguyễn Văn Tư at 19:00 and 21:00. One timetable. Vietnam Tourism says cycling is the way through the groves and that most hotels lend bicycles. It does not name a rental shop. Use a taxi meter, and bargain a xe ôm. The tourism office at 108/1 đường 30/4 is an office, not a station. Phường 4 on that line is a pre-December 2024 name.

The Đồng Khởi relic is a second morning, not the boat. The national extract sends you across Cầu Hàm Luông on Quốc lộ 57, more than 10 km to thị trấn Mỏ Cày Nam, then left about 4 km. A travel page says about 15 km from the city. The route and the 15 km both stand. Do not add them into one distance. Cầu Hàm Luông is the river south of town. It is not Cầu Rạch Miễu.

stayAreas.name: The town bank
stayAreas.summary: A river room on the town bank, so the evening is Hồ Trúc Giang, the parks, and the night market.

stayAreas.name: A garden on a near islet
stayAreas.summary: A garden homestay where the site sends the town boats, under the old names Mỹ Thạnh An and Phú Nhuận, or a house on Cồn Phụng if the night is the orchard rather than the lake. No brand.

eat: Breakfast on đường 30 Tháng 4 is hủ tiếu with a pork-pâté slice the provincial site calls local. Vietnam Tourism describes a dinner bowl of the same noodle with pork, shrimp, a quail egg, lime, and cilantro. Keep both plates. Do not fold the pâté into the quail-egg bowl. The street is the area.

Lunch on the boat is the garden table. The national rural page lists đuông dừa fried in butter, cá tai tượng chiên xù, xôi chiên phồng, lẩu mắm, cơm trái dừa, and tép rang dừa. Vietnam Tourism names creamy coconut rice, coconut-braised shrimp, and a light salad of củ hủ dừa. The provincial site, 4 June 2021, says that salad as gỏi củ hủ dừa tôm thịt. The 4 November 2021 overview adds nấm mối xào nước cốt dừa, ốc len xào dừa, and bánh xèo ốc gạo. The town-boat lunch adds dê hấp tía tô, lẩu gà lá giang, and ốc bươu nướng tiêu xanh. Kẹo dừa is warm at the kiln or wrapped to take home. Vietnam Tourism calls the plain piece coconut milk and sugar and says more than 300 factories. The provincial site, 25 November 2024, says coconut milk, maltose, and yellow cane sugar, and more than 180 workshops. Honey tea, a young coconut, and dừa nước are the drinks.

Bánh tráng Mỹ Lồng is rice paper from sticky rice and coconut milk, with sugar, salt, sesame, and sometimes milk or egg. The site gives two origins and does not choose: elders say about 100 years, and another story ties the dry rations to the Nguyễn–Trịnh years. Bánh phồng Sơn Đốc is glutinous rice pounded with coconut milk and sugar, then grilled so the cracker puffs to 3–4 times its size. The same page says the craft is more than 100 years old and began as a Tết offering, and quotes 51 households, about 25 million crackers a year, and a cooperative of 20 members. Both were listed as national intangible heritage by Quyết định số 4069/QĐ-BVHTTDL on 30 October 2018. Grill the paper or the cracker, or carry them home. The yards run all year and longer near Tết.
interestsBody: Give the morning to a boat on the Tiền. Cồn Phụng is the orchard gate. Cù lao Long is the short ferry past the market. Cồn Quy is longan. Lân has no bank named. The four nicknames are not one island, and Cồn Phụng is not cù lao Thới Sơn.

The palms are the crop: 53,000 ha, more than 60,000 ha, above 62,000 ha, and over 200,000 ha on an undated English rural article. About 500 million nuts a year stand on the two tourism pages. After dinner the walk is Hồ Trúc Giang and the market street.

Keep Đồng Khởi at Định Thủy, and the memorial of Nguyễn Đình Chiểu at Ba Tri, for another morning. The sea districts are a wild shore: nearly 20 km of beach at Ba Tri, and 65 km for the old province. Those are not the same measurement. Chợ Lách is fruit and ornamental gardens.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: For the kiln and the garden lunch, not a ranked restaurant list.
body: Kẹo dừa is warm at the kiln or wrapped to take home. Vietnam Tourism calls the plain piece coconut milk and sugar and says more than 300 factories. The provincial tourism site, 25 November 2024, says coconut milk, maltose, and yellow cane sugar, and more than 180 workshops. The rural page shows the boil at Cồn Phụng and does not give a count. Xôi chiên phồng is on that same lunch list, with đuông dừa fried in butter, cá tai tượng chiên xù, lẩu mắm, cơm trái dừa, and tép rang dừa. The 4 November 2021 overview adds nấm mối xào nước cốt dừa, ốc len xào dừa, and bánh xèo ốc gạo.

Breakfast on đường 30 Tháng 4 is hủ tiếu with a pork-pâté slice. Vietnam Tourism describes a dinner bowl of the same noodle with pork, shrimp, a quail egg, lime, and cilantro. Keep both plates. Honey tea is the sit-down drink, and on the town boat the guest mixes trà mật ong phấn hoa.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: The kiln, xôi chiên phồng, and the garden plates.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: For the day market on the way toward the river, and the night street after the lake.
body: Vietnam Tourism puts Chợ Bến Tre on the cycle past the market and the Ben Tre River, before the short ferry to Cù lao Long. The photograph is the day-market front. It is not the night market.

After dinner the site walks Hồ Trúc Giang, công viên Bến Tre, công viên Trần Văn Ơn, and công viên Đồng Khởi, then chợ đêm Bến Tre and khu phố chợ Phú Khương. Clause 117 merges the old phường Phú Khương into a new phường Phú Khương with Phường 8, Phú Hưng, and Nhơn Thạnh. The site still calls the night street khu phố chợ Phú Khương.

cards.title: Chợ Bến Tre
cards.summary: The day hall on the way to the river. The night stalls are on Đại lộ Đồng Khởi.

interestGroups.title: The Tiền and the islets
interestGroups.summary: For a boat on this bank of the river, not a canal morning in Cần Thơ.
body: Cồn Phụng is the longer version of the river day. On the ground of Đạo Dừa you walk Tòa Bảo tháp, Sân Rồng with nine dragons for the nine Mekong mouths, and Cửu Trùng đài. The rural page adds coconut candy, rice paper, more than 500 shell-craft objects, honey tea, đờn ca tài tử, a horse cart under the palms, and a sampan in a nipa creek. The town boat is the shorter version: a nipa creek, a kiln, fruit in season, a sampan, and lunch under the palms, from bến tàu du lịch thành phố Bến Tre. That pier is not the Cồn Phụng wharf.

Cồn Quy is longan, honey tea, and a ditch you can bail for fish and cook. Do not reuse the Cồn Phụng distances. Cù lao Long is a morning bicycle past the Ben Tre Market and the Ben Tre River, then a short ferry. Lân has no bank named. Other islets on the Hàm Luông stay unnamed.

cards.title: Cồn Phụng
cards.summary: 12 km by road and 25 km by river, or about 10 km.

cards.title: Cồn Quy
cards.summary: Longan, honey tea, and a ditch you can bail for fish.

interestGroups.title: Xứ dừa
interestGroups.summary: For the palms, the kiln, and the two craft villages inland.
body: The rural page calls this the coconut country of Vietnam and says more than 60,000 ha and about 500 million nuts a year. The national extract says 53,000 ha, about a quarter of the country’s coconut land, and about 500 million nuts. Báo Đồng Khởi says the area was above 62,000 ha by the 2015 festival. An undated English article from the national rural tourism center says over 200,000 ha, nearly half of the country’s coconut land. All four areas stand. Candy, milk, oil, and shell craft are the products. Vietnam Tourism calls the plain candy coconut milk and sugar. The provincial tourism site, 25 November 2024, says coconut milk, maltose, and yellow cane sugar. Eat it warm at the kiln. The rural page says more than 500 coconut-shell objects.

Mỹ Lồng, old xã Mỹ Thạnh, huyện Giồng Trôm, is the rice-paper yard. Clause 92 merges Mỹ Thạnh, Thuận Điền, and Lương Phú into xã Lương Phú and does not erase the craft name. Sơn Đốc sits in xã Hưng Nhượng, with the work in the hamlets and ấp Hưng Bình named for the households. Clause 88 keeps the name Hưng Nhượng. The two yards are not the same visit. Both were listed as national intangible heritage by Quyết định số 4069/QĐ-BVHTTDL on 30 October 2018.

cards.title: Coconut country
cards.summary: A bicycle under coconut palms in Châu Thành. 53,000 ha, more than 60,000 ha, above 62,000 ha, and over 200,000 ha.

interestGroups.title: Nguyễn Đình Chiểu
interestGroups.summary: For the poet’s tomb at Ba Tri, on 1 July or on an ordinary day.
body: The tomb and memorial sit at old xã An Đức, 2 km from the center of thị trấn Ba Tri, on tỉnh lộ 885 through Giồng Trôm. Clause 83 merges thị trấn Ba Tri and the communes Vĩnh Hòa, An Đức, Vĩnh An, and An Bình Tây into xã Ba Tri and does not say the tomb moved. The culture department’s site says the Ministry of Culture and Information listed it a national historic relic on 27 April 1990, on 13,000 m². The birth date on that site is 1 July 1822. He was not born in Bến Tre. He lived and worked here.

The culture program runs 30 June–2 July, and the day itself is 1 July on the solar calendar. On an ordinary day the ground is still the visit. The program includes đờn ca tài tử, a costume play of Lục Vân Tiên and Kiều Nguyệt Nga, recited verse, drum, traditional martial arts, a feast, and yard games.

cards.title: The Ba Tri memorial
cards.summary: A national historic relic since 27 April 1990. The culture day is 1 July solar.

interestGroups.title: A family on the water
interestGroups.summary: For the boat, the sampan, and the kiln, with the water park only after that.
body: The family day is the boat, the sampan in a nipa creek, and the candy kiln. A horse cart runs under the palms on Cồn Quy. After dark a motorboat runs along bần and nipa, with young coconut and fruit on board and fireflies in the creeks. Đờn ca tài tử at the garden stop has no separate ticket.

TTC Mekong Aqua Park, at 547D Nguyễn Đình Chiểu, ấp Phú Chiến, xã Phú Hưng, is the afternoon extra, with Tiny Zoo and a lunch court beside it. Clause 117 does not name Nguyễn Đình Chiểu. The address stays 547D Nguyễn Đình Chiểu. It is a hot afternoon after the boat, not the reason to come.

cards.title: A horse cart on Cồn Quy
cards.summary: The family day on the water. The water park is the afternoon extra.

interestGroups.title: Đồng Khởi
interestGroups.summary: For the 17 January 1960 ground, on a morning that is not the boat.
body: The rising opened on the morning of 17 January 1960 at Đình Rắn and the Vàm Nước post, in old xã Định Thủy, huyện Mỏ Cày Nam. The heritage page says Mỏ Cày Nam. The national extract says the same old district. Clause 70 merges Định Thủy, Phước Hiệp, and Bình Khánh into xã Đồng Khởi and does not say the house moved. Nhà truyền thống opened on 17 January 2000, nearly 5,000 m², on the old province-chief compound. The torch is 12 m high and 4.5 m across, with three wings. Đình Rắn, also called đình Định Nhơn, is 500 m northeast, rebuilt in 2005, 11 m by 25 m. The eight gold characters on the stone, from Hồ Chí Minh, read “Anh dũng Đồng Khởi, thắng Mỹ diệt ngụy”.

No ticket and no visit length were on the heritage page. The anniversary gatherings use 17 January. The road is across Cầu Hàm Luông on Quốc lộ 57, more than 10 km to thị trấn Mỏ Cày Nam, then left about 4 km, or about 15 km from the city. Do not add those into one distance. Công viên Đồng Khởi in town is not this house. Bảo tàng Bến Tre is 146 Hùng Vương. One travel page says 07:00–17:00 every day. Another says 07:30–11:00 and 13:30–17:00.

cards.title: The Định Thủy relic
cards.summary: Across Cầu Hàm Luông, more than 10 km then about 4 km, or about 15 km from the city.

cards.title: Bảo tàng Bến Tre
cards.summary: 146 Hùng Vương. The French front and the coconut-wood instruments, before the boat.

faqs.q: How far is Ben Tre from Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: The investment sheet says 86 km and 1.5 hours by car on the Ho Chi Minh City–Trung Lương expressway. Vietnam Tourism says about two hours. A travel page says about 85 km and about 2 hours. A car-hire page says 85–90 km and 1.5–2 hours.

faqs.q: How far is Cồn Phụng, and what is the gate?
faqs.a: The national rural page says 12 km by road and 25 km by river from the city center. The operator page says about 10 km. The town orchard pier is a different landing.

faqs.q: Which province is this, and how big is it?
faqs.a: Clause 20 of Nghị quyết 202/2025/QH15, as given by VOV, joins Bến Tre, Trà Vinh, and Vĩnh Long into the new Vĩnh Long province, 6,296.20 km² and 4,257,581 people, beside Đồng Tháp, Cần Thơ, and the sea. The investment sheet still gives the old province at 2,379.7 km² and 1,299,328 people, with Tiền Giang to the north, Trà Vinh to the south, Vĩnh Long to the west, and the sea to the east. The provincial tourism overview of 4 November 2021 says 2,394.82 km² and about 1.3 million people. Both of those are the pre-merger province. Article 2 tells the Government to fix the boundary. The clause does not name a capital.

The national extract says the coconut festival is held every two years around 30 April. Báo Đồng Khởi, 27 March 2019, lists 2009, 2010, 2012, 2015, and a fifth edition then planned for November 2019. Those lists do not match. The culture day at the poet’s memorial is 1 July, with a program from 30 June to 2 July. Đồng Khởi gatherings use 17 January. Nghinh Ông is the 15th and 16th of the sixth lunar month, and the fruit fair is Tết Đoan Ngọ on the 5th of the fifth lunar month. The solar days move.

season.label: Mild year-round
season.note: The national rural page says the weather is mild year-round and does not give a rainy month. VOV, 16 November 2024, reports a provincial directive for the dry season 2024–2025: salinity could reach the rivers from the second half of December 2024 and peak about February and March 2025. That is one season’s forecast. VOV, 6 October 2024, reports rain flooding nearly 0.5 m deep on Quốc lộ 57B near Khu công nghiệp Giao Long. That is not a closure of the Rạch Miễu crossing. The coconut festival is every two years around 30 April on the national extract, and 2009, 2010, 2012, 2015, plus a fifth edition then planned for November 2019, on Báo Đồng Khởi. The culture day is 1 July. Đồng Khởi uses 17 January.
